Rs. 44,745/- with interest and the liability to pay the compensation was fixed upon the present appellants.
2.

Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the .
present appeal are that a claim petition was preferred by one Sh. Pratap Singh, respondent No.1,
before this Court, on the ground that on 06.11.2008 he had engaged pick up bearing Registration No. HP-64-0434, owned by appellant Hira Singh and driven by appellant Dhanvir Singh, for carriage of sand and cement and other building materials from Sarahan to his native place.
As per the claimant he was sitting in the vehicle as the owner of the goods.
The vehicle met with an accident on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver and rolled down a cliff which resulted in claimant suffering multiple injuries.
He remained admitted in the hospital with effect from 06.11.2008 to 09.11.2008 and spent huge amount on his treatment.
He also suffered loss of income on account of the accident etc.

He claimed compensation to the tune of Rs.
5,00,000/-.
The respondents in the claim petition were the present appellants, who were impleaded therein as respondents No.1 and 2 respectively.
Respondent-Company was impleaded as respondent No.3.

The appellants herein admitted that the claimant had hired the vehicle but it was denied by them that the accident took place on account of rash .
and negligent driving on the part of the driver.
The stand of the Insurance Company was that the vehicle was being plied in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

The driver of the vehicle did not possess any valid and effective driving license and the injured was a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle and thus not covered in terms of the insurance policy.
There was violation of Section 157 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

3. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
"1. Whether Pratap Singh sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent No.2 on 06.11.2008 at about 10:45 AM near Baseach (lehar) Tehsil Pachhad, as alleged?
OPP 2.
In case issue No.1 is determined in affirmative to what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled to and from whom?
OPP 3.

Whether the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving license and that the vehicle was being plied in violation of the terms and Hira Singh And Another vs Partap Singh And Another on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81151995/
2 conditions of the insurance policy, as alleged ? OPR 4.

sentences.text: Whether the petition has been filed in collusion with respondents No.1 & 2, as alleged?

OPR . 
5. Whether the petitioner was travelling as a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle, as alleged?
OPR 6. Relief."

4. On the evidence led by the parties in support of their respective contentions, the issues were decided as under:-
 "Issue No.1 : Yes,
 Issue No.2 : Yes, Rs. 44,745/- as per operative  portion of the award.
 Issue No.3 : No  Issue No.4 : No  Issue No.5 : Yes.
 Issue No.6 : Petition allowed as per operative  portion of the award."
5.

Learned Tribunal thus held that the accident did take place on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle in which the claimant had sustained injuries and taking into consideration the factors pleaded by the claimant, it held the claimant entitled to compensation to the tune of Rs. 44,745/-.

On the issue as to whether the claimant was travelling as a gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle, learned Tribunal held that it was the pleaded case of the claimant as well as the appellants herein .
that the claimant was travelling in the offending vehicle as the owner of the goods loaded therein but in the evidence, it had come that the claimant was travelling in the vehicle as a labourer for loading and unloading of the goods therein.
Learned Tribunal held that similar statement was made by respondent No.2 before it when he stepped into the witness box as RW-1.
It thereafter held that it is settled law that a party to the civil proceedings is required to prove its case as set of in the pleadings and no evidence beyond the pleadings can be accepted.

In the case in hand, the claimant and respondents No.1 and 2 has amended their pleadings to clarify that the petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle as labourer and not as owner of the goods and in view of the conflicting stand taken by the claimant Hira Singh And Another vs Partap Singh And Another on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81151995/
3

sentences.text: and respondents No.1 and 2, they failed to show that the petitioner was travelling as a authorized passenger in the offending vehicle.
On these basis learned Tribunal decided issue No.5 in favour of the respondent- Company and against the present appellants.

6. I have heard learned Counsel for the parties and have also careful gone through the Award as well as the record .
of the case.
7. In fact, a perusal of the record of the case demonstrates that in terms of the claim petition, the owner of the vehicle was Hira Singh and the same was being driven by Dhanvir Singh.

A perusal of the reply filed to the claim petition by the Insurance Company demonstrates that in the preliminary submissions, an objection was raised by the Company to the effect that the ownership of the vehicle was transferred and no intimation was given to the insurance company in terms of Section 157 of the Motor Vehicle Act and, therefore, there was no enforceable contract between respondent No.1 in the claim petition and the Insurance Company on the date of the accident.

As already observed herein,
according to the claimant, the owner of the vehicle was Hira Singh.
Reply filed to the claim petition on behalf of Hira Singh demonstrates that he did not deny this fact before the learned Tribunal.

Now in this backdrop when one peruses the insurance policy and the insurance cover, which are on record and duly exhibitted, one finds that as on the date, when the accident took place, the vehicle was insured in the name of one Sh. Dhanvir Singh son .
of Sh. Krishan Singh, resident of V.P.O Jehar, Tehsil pachhad, District Sirmaur, H.P.

In other words,
the vehicle was not insured in the name of Sh. Hira Singh, who as per the claimant was the owner of the vehicle, as on the date, when the accident took place.

8. rSection 157 of the Motor Vehicle Act provides that where a person, in whose favour the certificate of insurance has been issued, transfers to another person the ownership of the motor vehicle, in respect of which such insurance was taken together with the policy of insurance thereto, the certificate of insurance and policy, described in the certificate, shall be deemed to have been transferred in favour of the person to whom the motor vehicle is transferred, with effect from the date of its transfer, with the condition that the transferre shall apply within 14 days from the date of transfer, in the prescribed form to the insurer for making necessary changes in respect to the fact of transfer in the certificate of the insurance and the policy described in the certificate in his favour.
9.

Now, in this case, there is nothing on record, from .
which it can be asserted as to when the vehicle was purchased by Hira Singh from its original owner.

Despite the fact that a preliminary submission was made in the reply filed by the Insurance Company about the violation of the provisions of Section 157 of the Motor Vehicle Act, no explanation came forth qua this particular preliminary submission from Sh. Hira Singh, who was impleaded as the owner of the vehicle in the claim petition.

This means that there was an implied Hira Singh And Another vs Partap Singh And Another on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81151995/
4 admission on part of Hira Singh about the non compliance of the provisions of Section 157 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

sentences.text: That being the case, therefore, as on the date, when the accident took place as there was no insurance of the offending vehicle, in the name of Sh. Hira Singh, there was no occasion for the compensation to be ordered to be indemnified by the Insurance Company, for the liability so fixed on Hira Singh and Dhanvir Singh.

Thereafter, as this Court also is of the considered view that liability as fastened by the learned Tribunal could not have been shifted upon the Insurance Company, in the light of the observations made herein above, this appeal being devoid of any merit is dismissed.

Pending miscellaneous applications, if .
any, also stand disposed of.
